findings.locator: PDF p3 / printed p2, General Differentiation Formulas
findings.source_claim: Lists sum, constant multiple, product, quotient and chain rules without local hypotheses.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Assume the constituent functions are differentiable at the relevant points, c is constant, and v is nonzero for the quotient.
findings.checked_deduction: The quotient equals u times v^-1 only where v is nonzero. Chain rule requires u differentiable at x and f differentiable at u(x). Every printed algebraic rule is correct under these standard conditions.

findings.locator: PDF p3 / printed p2, implicit cubic example final fraction
findings.source_claim: Gives yprime=-3y^2/(3y^2+6xy) without discussing its zero denominator.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Use on a local differentiable branch with 3y^2+6xy nonzero. The source curve has a vertical tangent where this denominator vanishes.
findings.checked_deduction: On F=y^3+3xy^2-8=0, y cannot be0. Fy=3y(y+2x)=0 implies y=-2x and4x^3=8, hence x=cuberoot(2), y=-2cuberoot(2). Fx=3y^2 is nonzero there, so a finite yprime is impossible. Away from that point the printed formula follows exactly from Fx+Fy yprime=0.

findings.locator: PDF p3 / printed p2, final inverse-sine derivation
findings.correction_or_qualification: Specify principal arcsin with y in[-pi/2,pi/2] and |x|<1 for the finite derivative.
findings.checked_deduction: cos(y) is the positive square root on the principal interior branch. Other local inverse branches may have negative cosine; endpoints x=+/-1 have no finite ordinary derivative. Thus the displayed positive formula is correct only with the intended branch/domain.

findings.locator: PDF p4 / printed p3, both real-power proofs
findings.source_claim: Uses x=e^(ln x), ln(f)=r ln(x), and (ln f)prime=fprime/f without stating positivity.
findings.correction_or_qualification: For the displayed proof take x>0 and fixed real r, so f=x^r>0. General logarithmic differentiation of a nonzero real f can use ln|f|.
findings.checked_deduction: Real ln(x) requires x>0. Arbitrary irrational powers have no standard real definition on a negative open interval; selected rational/integer powers can have wider domains but these logarithmic lines do not establish those cases. Both printed derivations are correct on x>0.

findings.locator: PDF p4 / printed p3, trigonometric limit and derivative formulas
findings.source_claim: Uses lim sin(h)/h=1 and the unscaled trigonometric derivatives.
findings.correction_or_qualification: State that arguments are measured in radians.
findings.checked_deduction: With a degree-valued argument t, sin_degrees(t)=sin(pi t/180), so the corresponding limit and derivative acquire pi/180. The displayed formulas are correct with the standard radian convention.

independent_checks.check: Entire attribution/cover page read and visually inspected; no mathematical figure/equation.

Checked exponential definitions, both hyperbolic derivatives and complete expansion of cosh^2-sinh^2=1. Mixed terms reduce to(2+2)/4. Parameterization u=cosh(t),v=sinh(t) lies on the right branch u>=1 of u^2-v^2=1; the source correctly identifies the hyperbola equation and does not assert both branches are traced. Circular identity and comparison are correct.

Independently derived quotient from product and reciprocal chain rule. Cubic differentiation gives3y^2 yprime+3y^2+6xy yprime=0, correct. Computed exceptional vertical-tangent point and principal inverse-sine domain as recorded. No graph on this page.

secprime=sin(x)/cos^2(x)=tan(x)sec(x) wherever cos(x) is nonzero. The two supplied limits plus angle-addition formulas yield sinprime=cos and cosprime=-sin in radians. Difference-quotient definition is correct when the limit exists. Both real-power arguments give r x^(r-1) on x>0.

Product/chain differentiation of exp(x arctan x) gives exp(x arctan x)[arctan x+x/(1+x^2)], exactly as printed, for every real x. Parentheses/exponent placement confirmed in the page image. No demonstrated formula error found in this lecture.
